clue.text: Fish course taken by motorist on a long run?

parts.note: the cod is a common food fish
a river runs in a course, so a watercourse stands for it

explanation.surface: Someone on a long drive stops for a fish dish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fish course' looks like a menu item, but it splits into two pieces. A co-driver shares the wheel on a long journey or rally.
explanation.definitionFit: A co-driver takes turns at the wheel with another driver, typical of long rallies.

clue.text: Evil article on the place of war

indicators.note: in a down clue, on puts the article below the evil

parts.note: a crime is an evil act
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A grim newspaper item about a battleground.
explanation.walkthrough: The Crimean War (1853-56) was fought on this peninsula.
explanation.definitionFit: The Black Sea peninsula was the scene of the Crimean War.

clue.text: Application for a coach

explanation.surface: Someone applying for a coaching job.
explanation.definitionFit: Diligence is careful application to work; a diligence was also a French public stagecoach.

clue.text: Outgoing children

explanation.surface: Sociable kids.
explanation.definitionFit: An issue is an outflow or emergence, and also offspring, a family's descendants.

clue.text: Listener's complaint

parts.note: a listener is literally an ear, and a complaint here is an ailment, not a grumble

explanation.surface: Someone in an audience grumbles.
explanation.definitionFit: Pain in the ear is the ailment that afflicts the organ of hearing.

clue.text: Do wrong from start to finish

parts.note: 'they're off' marks the start of a race, so off means start
an end is a finish

explanation.surface: Doing wrong all the way through, beginning to end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' and 'to' are link words framing the two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: To offend is to commit a wrong or transgress.

clue.text: Auspicious yet strange turn o' fate

indicators.note: strange suggests the letters of the phrase take an odd new order

explanation.surface: A lucky but odd twist of destiny.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strange' rearranges TURN O FATE.
explanation.definitionFit: Lucky, favoured by good omens, which is what auspicious implies.

clue.text: Choose to take a seat

explanation.surface: Deciding to sit down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'take a seat' looks like sitting down; it means winning a seat in parliament.
explanation.definitionFit: To elect is to pick; an elected member is voted in to take a parliamentary seat.

clue.text: Stride about on the ship when there's trouble

indicators.note: in a down clue, on puts the ship below the rearranged letters
about suggests the letters of the word are moved around

parts.note: SS stands for steamship

explanation.surface: Someone paces the deck when trouble strikes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' rearranges STRIDE into DISTRE; 'the' and 'when there's' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: Distress is suffering or difficulty, as in a ship in danger.

clue.text: Your ills may turn out to be imaginary

indicators.note: turn out suggests the letters of the words before it end up rearranged in a new form

explanation.surface: A reassurance that your ailments may all be in your head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turn out' rearranges YOUR and ILLS.
explanation.definitionFit: Something illusory is deceptive and unreal, existing only in the mind.

clue.text: Feeling of revulsion goes slowly

explanation.surface: A sense of disgust that drags along.
explanation.definitionFit: 'The creeps' is the shudder of revulsion; to creep is to move stealthily and slowly.

clue.text: Game in which all matches are exciting

definitions.text: Game in which all matches are exciting

parts.words: Game in which all matches are exciting
parts.note: a card game whose whole point is spotting a pair of identical cards, so every match is the moment of excitement

explanation.surface: A sporting fixture list where every contest thrills.
explanation.definitionFit: The children's card game in which players call out when two matching cards appear.

clue.text: High-flier gets a good score on the course

definitions.text: a good score on the course

explanation.surface: An ambitious golfer posts a fine round.
explanation.definitionFit: A bird of prey soaring high; in golf, two under par on a hole.

clue.text: Musical live-wire

parts.note: an energetic person in music who leads the orchestra, and also something that carries current like a live wire

explanation.surface: A lively, energetic musician.
explanation.definitionFit: Both the orchestra leader with a baton and a material carrying electric current share this name.

clue.text: Supply with power?

parts.note: reads as connecting electricity, but means giving someone the means or authority to do something

explanation.surface: A question about providing electricity.
explanation.definitionFit: To give the capacity or authority to act is to empower someone.

clue.text: Glass or beer-mat needs changing

indicators.note: needs changing suggests the letters of the words are to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A pub scene: the drink or its coaster needs replacing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Glass' looks like a drinking glass but is the weather glass; 'needs changing' rearranges OR BEERMAT.
explanation.definitionFit: A weather glass is an old name for an instrument measuring air pressure.

clue.text: Tells of twinges after exercise

indicators.note: after places the pains following the exercise in the answer

parts.note: PE is physical education, school exercise
aches are twinges of pain

explanation.surface: Someone complains of pains after a workout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tells' is a verb: to peach is old slang for informing on someone.
explanation.definitionFit: To peach on an accomplice is to inform on them, a slang sense of betraying.

clue.text: Break one's word?

parts.note: reads as failing a promise, but means splitting a word with a dash

explanation.surface: Asking whether someone has gone back on a promise.
explanation.definitionFit: To divide a word into parts with a short dash, as at a line end.

clue.text: Safe in vile jail

indicators.note: in puts one word inside the other

parts.note: base means vile, low
a till is a cash drawer, a safe place for a shop's money

explanation.surface: Locked in a strongbox inside a filthy prison.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Safe' looks like a hiding place for the jailbird; it is the shop's TILL, which goes inside BASE. The Bastille was the notorious Paris prison stormed in 1789.
explanation.definitionFit: The Paris fortress used as a state prison, and by extension any prison.

clue.text: Declared a number were incorrect

parts.note: V is the Roman numeral five
erred means were mistaken

explanation.surface: Someone stated that a figure was wrong.
explanation.definitionFit: To aver is to assert or state firmly.

clue.text: At short notice, come up with information

indicators.note: in a down clue, come up means the pieces read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: at taken as written
an ad is an advertisement, a notice shortened

explanation.surface: Producing facts at short notice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'come up' reverses AT + AD (ATAD), reading upwards in the grid.
explanation.definitionFit: Facts and figures, the raw material of information.

clue.text: Sound move, but plain to a Russian

indicators.note: sound tells us the word for a move is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: a step is a move made with the foot

explanation.surface: A good move, though a Russian sees it as obvious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plain' is the noun, flat grassland, not 'obvious'. The steppes are Russia's grassy plains.
explanation.definitionFit: The steppe is a vast treeless grassland of Russia and Central Asia.

clue.text: Plans for me to enter chess knock-out

indicators.note: to enter puts one piece inside another
knock-out suggests the letters of chess are knocked into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Scheming to get into a chess tournament.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knock-out' rearranges CHESS into SCHES, and ME goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Schemes are plans or strategies, sometimes devious ones.

clue.text: A letter, say, as an attachment

indicators.note: say tells us the phrase is spoken

parts.note: a letter of the alphabet, the one named 'ex', preceded by an

explanation.surface: Sending a letter as an email attachment.
explanation.walkthrough: Spoken, 'an X' gives the word.
explanation.definitionFit: An annexe is a building or document added on to a main one.

clue.text: Checkmate in sporting event

parts.note: check means test, as in checking something
mate means match, pair up

explanation.surface: A chess finish at a sporting occasion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Checkmate' splits into CHECK (test) and MATE (match). A test match is an international cricket match between national sides.
explanation.definitionFit: A test match is a full international fixture in cricket or rugby.

clue.text: Is getting up with fresh strength

indicators.note: in a down clue, getting up means reading upwards, so backwards

parts.note: fresh means new

explanation.surface: Rising with renewed vigour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting up' reverses IS to SI.
explanation.definitionFit: Sinew is a tendon, and figuratively muscular power.

clue.text: Woman gets directions in Polish

parts.note: she refers to a woman
E is east, a compass direction
N is north, another compass direction

explanation.surface: A woman receives instructions in the Polish language.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Polish' looks like the nationality but is the shine you give by polishing.
explanation.definitionFit: A sheen is a gloss or lustre, the result of polishing.

clue.text: One aims to look through it

definitions.text: One aims to look through it

parts.words: One aims to look through it
parts.note: a gunner squints through this when aiming, though it reads like someone hoping to glance over a document

explanation.surface: Someone intends to skim a document.
explanation.definitionFit: The aiming device on a gun or telescope that one peers along.

clue.text: A good one is important to one bowling from end to end

definitions.text: A good one is important to one bowling

explanation.surface: Advice to a bowler about where to pitch the ball.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket a good length is the ideal place to pitch a delivery; it also means distance measured end to end.

clue.text: Government leader in Arab state made to leave home

indicators.note: this word is a container marker: it says one piece is placed inside the other, and the clue words of the pieces show which way round

parts.note: an emirate is a state ruled by an emir

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its opening letter

explanation.surface: A political leader in a Gulf state is forced into exile.
explanation.walkthrough: 'made to' is a link. 'Government leader' is G, which goes in EMIRATE.
explanation.definitionFit: To emigrate is to leave one's country to settle abroad.

clue.text: He takes part in a spirited war-dance

indicators.note: takes part in says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A man joins in a lively war dance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'He' stands for a male name; the run spans spiritED WAR-Dance.
explanation.definitionFit: A man's first name, so 'he' can stand for one such male person.

clue.text: We are its new version, so to speak

indicators.note: a new version of the words reworks their letters into a different order

explanation.surface: A self-referential claim to be a fresh edition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new version' rearranges WE ARE ITS.
explanation.definitionFit: Both phrases hedge a figurative expression, meaning in a manner of speaking.
